newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta government to take control of Malta Drydocks.
newsitem.headline: Malta government to take control of Malta Drydocks.

text.p: The Maltese government said Friday it would take more direct control of the loss-making Malta Drydocks.

Prime Minister Alfred Sant told parliament that the council that runs the state-owned yard will be reconstituted. Four members would be elected by dock workers, while another four members and the chairman would be appointed by the government.
The council has since 1975 been wholly composed of dockyard workers directly elected by the dockyard's 3,500 workforce.
The Drydocks Council said that it was against any government representation.
A recent report said that the government had lost control and influence in the running of the yard and it was only serving to prop it up financially.
The government-commissioned report said many members of the council lacked managerial knowhow and the dockyard's professional management was often bypassed.
Sant said his government had inherited an unacceptable situation where the yard absorbed some 15 million Maltese pounds ($40.5 million) from government funds annually.
The government wanted the yard to change its management and financial structure and improve its marketing and sales, Sant said.
"The government has started a programme aimed at making Malta Drydocks the most modern and efficient dockyard in the Mediterranean" he said.
